The retina plays a vital role in vision, yet many retinal conditions develop silently and may not show symptoms until significant damage has occurred. Early diagnosis by a retina specialist can help protect vision and improve treatment outcomes.

Warning signs that need immediate attention:

• Sudden flashes of light
• New or increasing floaters
• Blurred or distorted vision
• A dark curtain or shadow in vision
• Difficulty reading or recognising faces
• Sudden vision loss

Common retina disorders include diabetic retinopathy, retinal detachment, macular degeneration, macular holes, and retinal tears. Many of these conditions respond better when diagnosed and treated early.

At ASG Eye Hospital, advanced retinal imaging and modern diagnostic technology help specialists detect retinal problems accurately and recommend the most appropriate retina treatment.

Available treatment options may include:

• Retinal laser treatment
• Intravitreal injections
• Vitrectomy surgery

Delaying treatment can increase the risk of permanent vision loss. If you notice any sudden changes in your eyesight, seeking prompt evaluation from a qualified retina specialist is essential.

Book your retina consultation at ASG Eye Hospital today and take the first step toward protecting your vision.

Diabetes can affect your eyesight without obvious warning signs. Many people with diabetic eye disease experience no symptoms until retinal damage has already begun. Regular eye examinations are essential for protecting long-term vision.

Common symptoms to watch for include:

• Blurred or fluctuating vision
• Floaters or dark spots
• Difficulty reading
• Distorted vision
• Poor night vision
• Sudden vision changes

One of the most common diabetes-related eye conditions is diabetic retinopathy, which affects the blood vessels in the retina. Early detection through retinal screening can help prevent serious vision complications.

Protect your eye health by:

• Maintaining healthy blood sugar levels
• Monitoring blood pressure regularly
• Taking medications as prescribed
• Staying physically active
• Avoiding tobacco use

Frequently Asked Questions at Amavi Eye Clinic

Planning a visit to our center in Borivali West? Here is what patients ask us most frequently about our eye care services:

🗓️ What should I bring to my consultation?
Please bring any previous eye reports, your current prescription glasses, and a list of any ongoing medications you take.

⏳ How long does a routine check-up take?
A comprehensive vision test and eye exam typically take 30 to 45 minutes. If your consultation requires pupil dilation for a deeper evaluation, please plan for up to 2 hours.

👁️ What happens during a routine eye exam?
We perform a complete vision test alongside refraction to check your glasses prescription. Dr. Ami Shah also conducts an eye pressure check and a detailed slit-lamp examination to evaluate both the anterior and interior health of your eyes.

🏥 What medical and surgical services are available?
With over 10 years of experience, Dr. Ami Shah provides complete care including modern laser vision correction, advanced micro-incision cataract surgery with premium lens options, and comprehensive glaucoma screenings. We also specialize in dry eye treatment and routine pediatric eye evaluations.

Eyecare tips in summer.

During Summers, a mix of heat, dust and dehydration can cause several eye issues. 
Here are some tips which can help prevent eye issues. 

1. Don’t skip sunglasses
Go for sunglasses that block 99–100% of UV rays. Prolonged UV exposure can increase the risk of conditions like cataracts and photokeratitis. 

2.Stay hydrated
Your eyes rely on proper tear production. Dehydration can worsen dryness and irritation, sometimes leading to dry eye syndrome.

3.Limit direct sun exposure
Try to avoid peak sunlight hours (roughly 11 AM–4 PM). Wearing a hat or sunglasses will protect your eyes.

4.Protect against dust and pollution
If you’re outdoors a lot, especially in windy or dusty areas, use protective eyewear. Dust can trigger allergies. 

5.Use lubricating eye drops (if needed)
Artificial tears can help keep your eyes moist, especially if you spend time in air-conditioned rooms.
